challenges.name: Consent Granted
challenges.description:
An employee reported a suspicious email asking them to approve an application. Investigate the AuditLogs to find which application received an illicit consent grant.

Submit the application's display name as your flag.

hints.content: Look for AuditLogs where OperationName == 'Consent to application'. Check the TargetResources for the app name.

challenges.name: The Proxy in the Middle
challenges.description:
A user completed MFA successfully but their account was compromised. The attacker used an adversary-in-the-middle proxy to steal the session cookie.

Find the sign-in where the session was replayed and submit the attacker's IP address as your flag.

hints.content: Look for a successful MFA sign-in followed by token use from a different IP within a short time window. Compare the IP addresses.
Join SigninLogs (MFA event) with AADNonInteractiveUserSignInLogs (token replay) on UserPrincipalName and filter where IPs don't match.

challenges.name: Enter the Code
challenges.description:
An attacker used a device code phishing attack to compromise a user's account. The user doesn't normally use device code authentication.

1. Find the device code sign-in event
2. Trace the attacker's subsequent access

Submit the first Azure resource the attacker accessed after the device code authentication as your flag.

hints.content: Filter SigninLogs for AuthenticationProtocol == 'deviceCode' and look for users who don't normally use this flow.

challenges.name: Full Chain

hints.content: You need to query multiple tables: AuditLogs for consent, SigninLogs for AiTM and device code. Build a union of the earliest indicators from each attack type.

challenges.name: Build the Detection
challenges.description:
Write a Sentinel analytics rule (KQL query) that would detect ONE of the three phishing techniques covered in this module. The query must:

1. Return results within 5 minutes of the attack occurring
2. Include the UserPrincipalName and IPAddress in the output
3. Have a false-positive rate below 5% (explain your tuning logic)

Submit the SHA256 hash of your KQL query (no whitespace) as your flag.

Note: This is a manually graded challenge. Submit your query to the instructor for review.

hints.content: Focus on the technique with the clearest signal-to-noise ratio. Device code phishing often has the lowest false-positive rate because so few legitimate users use it.
